title: Finite reductions detect integral constructible isomorphisms
statement: For the completed coefficient sheaf of a finite extension E of Q_l on any scheme Y, let M,N be integral constructible objects [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. If every finite derived scalar reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] of a morphism f:M→N is invertible, then f is invertible.

source.place: Finite reduction of the canonical completed-coefficient projection and conservativity of derived-complete objects.

proof.text: Take a distinguished cone of f. Integral constructibles form a triangulated subcategory, so the cone is derived complete.
Derived reduction is exact; its cone triangle has invertible first arrow, hence zero third object. Exact restriction of scalars preserves its zero object.
Each factor of the canonical augmented Roos product is zero. Product extensionality kills both product objects, and the completeness triangle kills the cone. Therefore f is invertible.
